description.purpose: Context assembly as a hive: the orchestrator that decides what enters an LLM's context window and what leaves it. A rolling short-term conversation window (user and assistant turns, session-scoped, store-backed), the memory bundle, the tool round fanned back in, and a cap over every one of those three legs that is deterministic configuration rather than a model judgement. Everything the brain sees leaves through ONE message on one route - and the same seam ends a runaway tool round and hands a closed session on as one batch, so a later split of the agent behind that seam does not re-cut the collector. A round that loses a tool result exits deterministically past an idle window (synthetic error results, round_stale=1), and a user turn arriving mid-round defers instead of opening a second brain call - decided behaviour where there used to be accident. Since 1.1.0 the window is also CURATED: a budget projection that runs at every assembly - not at a threshold - and replaces tool payloads it cannot afford with stubs that carry a recovery key, in declared stages, without a single model call. What it may take is declared per tool name; everything undeclared is unique and is never touched, so an undeclared tool costs context and never correctness. The conversation, system.*, the tool_call names and the newest rounds are out of reach at every stage, which is why the same question has the same answer basis before and after any number of curations - the property a prose fold cannot have, because this one rewrites no text at all. `thread_recall` is the way back: the collector serves it itself, out of its own slate, uncapped, behind a per-turn budget wall. Housekeeping is evidence-gated: the close batch writes a delivery ledger row, and only ledger-named, aged sessions are ever pruned - on an operator lane the template never fires itself.
description.use_when: One per agent brain, between the inbound surface and the LLM. It replaces the pattern where a persona cell injects the system prompt, a prep cell mints the turn id and a third cell fans tool results in: those are one concern and this is it. Wire the eleven entry lanes and the exit routes in the SAME mutation that instantiates it - an island without a crossing edge stays inactive.
description.not_in_scope: No inference and no persona (identity is not context assembly). No tool fan-OUT: routing a tool_call to the right tool stays a dispatcher's job, the collector only fans the results back in - including the one tool it serves itself, memory_recall, which reaches it over an ordinary tool edge the dispatcher chose by name (GH #78). No session lifecycle: a keeper decides when a generation begins and ends, the collector consumes the session_id and answers the close request. No memory judgement: the collector READS the recall bundle and hands a closed session on unfiltered, but what is extracted and what is kept belongs to the receiver of the write batch. No LLM judgement anywhere - every cap is a number. No cap deletes: every cut is a read-time cut and the full value stays in the store; rows fall only on the in_prune lane, only for sessions whose close batch already left (the batched ledger row is the evidence) and only behind params.prune_after_ms - without that evidence the store grows rather than loses a turn, and the collector never schedules a prune itself. No second body format for a tool result: a result is the `tool_result` turns of its `messages[]` and nothing else. A `system` slot on the in_tool lane is dropped, and that is not an oversight (GH #252): `system.*` leaving the seam is upserted into the brain cell's own cell.db and outlives the round that wrote it, so nothing that is the evidence of ONE round belongs there. Since 2.1.0 that rule has no exception left - the memory bundle was the one carve-out and does not live in system.* either any more, it arrives as a synthetic memory_recall tool result inside the round it was fetched for, and what stays under system.memory is the revocation of that slot (GH #278).
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the HIVE path (`params.ports` is empty since GH #228; an edge naming ./assemble or ./window is refused with hive_port_boundary), and what a caller wants rides on hop.route. Entry (the parent edge names the lane via set_hop route and promotes session_id): in_turn (an inbound user turn), in_bundle (the memory hive's recall bundle), in_advice (an advisor core's answer, arriving after its turn ended), in_calls (the assistant tool_call turn from a dispatcher), in_tool (one tool result: every turn of its messages[], filed under the call id each turn answers -- a result that answers two calls in one message closes both, and a `system` slot or a top-level body slot on a result is dropped at the lane on purpose, GH #252), in_memory_call (a memory_recall tool_call the dispatcher routed by hop.tool_name - the collector serves it itself), in_thread_call (a thread_recall tool_call, likewise served here - it brings a payload the curator elided back out of THIS turn's own round table), in_answer (the brain's final turn), in_close (a session keeper's close request, hop.route == 'close'), in_prune (a timer's or operator's housekeeping request, hop.route == 'prune'), in_round_sweep (a timer's or operator's stuck-round re-check, hop.route == 'sweep'). Exit (from the hive path, on hop.route): 'brain' -> the agent LLM (promote hop.iter and hop.turn_id to context on that edge), 'answer' -> the reply sink, 'recall' -> the memory hive's recall port (the per-turn leg when params.memory_tier is set, and every memory_recall call; promote recall_query / memory_tier / memory_call_id / recall_window_from / recall_window_to / session_id / turn_id / iter), 'write' -> wherever a closed session belongs, 'turn_write' -> the SAME consumer after every stored turn (only with params.turn_write set: the day so far, so an episode exists at the turn instead of at the close - wire it to the same cell the write route feeds, never to a second one), 'prune' -> a log sink or the operator surface (one report per pruned session).
turn 3 of a session references turn 1: the window carries turns 1..3 into the context, so the answer does not depend on retrieval luck

params.window_turns=5 over a 40-turn session: the store returns the 5 newest, hop.window_capped=1; a byte cap that cannot afford the oldest of them drops it and everything older, hop.window_dropped counts them
2 parallel tool calls: 1 assistant row + 2 tool rows in the round table, the guarded update wins once, and the re-entry carries the window AND the tool round through the same seam
a tool that answers two calls in ONE message: both results are filed under their own tool_call_id, the round is complete and fires -- the lane keeps the whole messages[], not its first turn
a 100 KB tool result: params.tool_chars of it reach the seam with hop.round_capped=1, all of it stays readable in the round table
a model that will not stop asking for tools: at params.max_iter the seam emits route 'answer' with what it collected instead of a further brain call
the keeper closes a generation: one message on route 'write' with every turn of the session in order and every round row beside it, and the delivery ledger row written in the same multi-send

a timer fires the prune lane a week later: the delivered session's rows fall up to its close boundary, the living session keeps every byte, and the cut is reported on route 'prune' - without a ledger row the same request cuts nothing and says so

a tool dies mid-flight and one result never arrives: the round parks, and the next turn, the next result or an in_round_sweep request after params.round_idle_ms closes it - the missing call is answered synthetically under its own tool_call_id and the round fires with round_stale=1
a user turn lands while a round is running: it enters the window, defers (no second brain call on the session), and rides with the next regular assembly marked round_deferred=1

a tool loop over twenty large file reads: the curator elides the payloads of the declared-recoverable ones from every round older than params.keep_rounds, leaves a stub with a content hash and a thread_recall key in their place, and reports hop.curate_stage / hop.curate_elided / hop.curate_saved - no model was asked and no word was rewritten

the model needs an elided result back: it calls thread_recall(call_id) and gets the ORIGINAL text, uncapped, as a tool_result of the running round - over params.thread_recall_budget the call is refused with a typed error instead of being silently halved

the model wants memory about a TIME RANGE: it emits a memory_recall tool_call, the dispatcher routes it by hop.tool_name like any other tool, and the collector - which already owns the recall port - serves the call itself, passes the window on as recall_window_from/_to and answers under the original tool_call_id, so the round ends where it began (GH #78)
